triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The three rules applying the 12.5% forced-labor 301 duty to products of China under HTS 9903.05.31 started 2026-07-23, a day before the notice's entry-date gate of July 24, 2026.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 5 (China instead of Brazil); only effective_from lines changed, formulas and the 9903.05.85-9903.05.92 exception untouched. FR 2026-15181 DATES verified through the pinned corpus. Companion test unchanged.
triage.verifier_justification: The whole diff is three identical version-window edits — `effective_from` moved from '2026-07-23' to '2026-07-24' on all three rules (heading applicability, general rate, special rate) — with formulas, rates, inputs, outputs, proof atoms, and scope untouched, so it is a pure meaning change to the version window, not provenance bookkeeping. I attempted to refute it two ways and both failed: the pinned corpus text of the cited HTS heading (us/statute/hts/9903.05.31) carries no date at all, but the establishing notice it implements, FR 2026-15181 Annex I, reads "A. Effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026, subchapter III of chapter 99 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) is modified as follows: 1. The following new provisions are inserted" — so the heading did not exist for July 23 entries and the pre-fix encoding applied a 12.5% duty a day early. Nor is this a strictness error (effective_from stays an inclusive lower bound matching "on or after"), an amount change, or added coverage, so no other kind fits better than wrong_period_or_effective_date, and the PR itself had already flagged the mismatch as an open judgment call ("Forced-labor 301 component gated at ≥ 2026-07-24 per FR 2026-15181 DATES, although heading modules carry effective_from 2026-07-23").
triage.verifier_notes: Corroborating detail a reviewer may want: the companion module forced-labor-presidential-action.yaml deliberately KEEPS effective_from '2026-07-23' (the date of the presidential memorandum) in this same commit, while only the HTS heading modules move to 07-24 (the Annex I entry-date gate). That asymmetry is source-correct, not an inconsistency, and it rules out a "someone bulk-shifted dates" reading. Two things stop short of refuting but are worth recording: (1) the module's own declared corpus_citation_path is the dateless HTS article description, so the date's grounding lives in FR 2026-15181 (cited in the composition, not in this module's proof atoms) — a provenance gap, not a misclassification; (2) the composition already gated the forced-labor 301 component at >= 2026-07-24, so the composed program's numbers likely did not change — the defect was latent in the module's standalone meaning. Also note the companion test file was not touched: all three cases run at 2026-08-01, so no case exercises the 07-23/07-24 boundary and the defect could not have been caught by the module's own tests. Separately unrepresented (and not addressed by this fix): the FR's in-transit carve-out exempting goods loaded before 07-24 and entered before 07-28.
